headline: Denmark's outgoing Speaker says he has 'powerful enemies' in his own party
deck: A newspaper portrait built on 13 anonymous sources called him vain and lazy; the prime minister calls such attacks 'beneath contempt'.
standard: Søren Gade, who left the post of Speaker of Denmark's parliament on Tuesday, says he has 'powerful enemies in Venstre', a liberal party and his own. He was answering a portrait in Jyllands-Posten, a Danish daily newspaper, in which 13 anonymous sources called him vain, disloyal, selfish, lazy and greedy.

Mette Frederiksen, the prime minister, called anonymous attacks by elected politicians 'beneath contempt'; Troels Lund Poulsen, Venstre's leader, called the piece 'an unusually sad and nasty portrait'.
The newspaper amended the portrait on Tuesday, saying its first version was 'not sufficiently balanced'; its political editor stands '100 per cent' behind the original.
short: Søren Gade, who left the post of Speaker of Denmark's parliament on Tuesday, says he has 'powerful enemies in Venstre', a liberal party and his own. Jyllands-Posten, a Danish daily newspaper, had printed a portrait in which 13 anonymous sources called him vain and lazy; it has since amended it.
